> `missionctl whoami` as this release renders it, with no installation behind it. Where this file and your server differ, the server is right.

# Who you are: `missionctl whoami`

One JSON document, `mc.whoami.v1`: the verified principal of the token in use and what this server composed. It reads nothing a request body says. Placeholders are in capitals.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "mc.whoami.v1",
  "actor_id": "ACTOR_ID",
  "application_id": "APPLICATION_ID",
  "installation_id": "INSTALLATION_ID",
  "tenant_id": "TENANT_ID",
  "request_scope": "REQUEST_SCOPE",
  "permissions": [
    "PERMISSION",
    "reviewer:ROLE"
  ],
  "authority_refs": [
    "AUTHORITY_REF"
  ],
  "sponsorship_refs": [
    "SPONSORSHIP_REF"
  ],
  "approval_refs": [
    "APPROVAL_REF"
  ],
  "reviewer_roles": [
    "ROLE"
  ],
  "reviews_as": [
    "ACTOR_ID",
    "ROLE"
  ],
  "server": {
    "time_travel": [
      {
        "lane_profile": "LANE_PROFILE",
        "declared_read": "LEVEL",
        "declared_fork": "LEVEL",
        "state_as_of": "not_composed",
        "prerequisite": "WHAT THE DEPLOYMENT MUST PROVIDE"
      }
    ],
    "external_discovery": "not_composed"
  }
}
```

- `server.time_travel[].state_as_of`: `readable`, `not_composed`, `not_declared`; `prerequisite` is present only where the state is not `readable`.
- `server.external_discovery`: `composed`, `not_composed`.
